1-0.tagline: Same pitch on stage. Only one works.

events.text: Stake on your own sleep or workouts. Your wearable proves it, and SPOTTER pays whoever hit. Open gohealthme.app; it's live.
Get paid in crypto for real workouts. AI plans your training, the camera counts your reps, and fans bet on who wins.
Show me a new user's first five minutes. Where can I try it?
On gohealthme.app: pick a challenge, stake test USDC, connect a wearable. Our live test ran all 8 demo steps on Windows, Android and iPhone.
Sign in with Self, get your AI plan, join a contest, start the camera. It's all in our demo video.
FitterCoin's live test paid a 0.00000001 ETH stake and escrowed nothing.

evidence.label: B · live test d6: tx confirmed, 0 ETH escrowed

events.text: The checks are off while we test. The flow is all there.

events.reason: The screens load, but the paid entry the pitch depends on is free.

events.text: Who stakes money on their sleep? That's a niche.
Anyone with a wearable who's broken a promise to themselves. 16 of 16 flows work today on every device we tested.

events.reason: The journey is clear and runs end to end on both devices.

events.text: Which screen does a user see most, and does it work on a phone?
The challenges list. Our Android and iPhone runs passed all 16 steps, with no sideways scroll.
The contest arena, built around the camera view.
FitterCoin's rep counter opens a desktop window at localhost:5001. A phone can't reach it.
Mobile is on our roadmap.

events.reason: The only rep counter is a desktop app. There's no phone path in the code.
Your UI breaks on mobile. Every demo frame is a desktop capture, and the camera only runs in a localhost window.

events.text: Show me the line where the money moves.
HealthPoolsV3.sol:300 pulls the stake. Payouts land in an owed[] ledger at line 115 and winners withdraw.
bet.sol settles spectator bets and contest.sol escrows the stakes.
FitterCoin's settle() is a view function. It can't pay anyone.
The settlement logic is written, just commented out while we tested.

events.reason: Commented-out code settles nothing: bet.sol:42-59 changes no state.

events.text: SPOTTER is one agent holding the payout keys. That's a single point of failure.
Owner, oracle and settler are three distinct keys, enforced at HealthPoolsV3.sol:180.

events.reason: Roles are split in code, but SPOTTER is still one operator.
That feature has no code behind it. Spectator betting is your headline, and settle() is an empty view.

events.text: What can you do that a step-counter app can't?
Money on the line, proof from the wearable, and your health data never touches the chain. Only the verdict does.
AI training plans, live rep counting and a betting arena, all in one app.
Stake-on-yourself apps exist. StickK did this in 2008.
StickK trusts your word. We settle on wearable proof, on chain, without your health data.

events.reason: Wearable-verified, private settlement is a real step past honour-system apps.

events.text: FitterCoin's AI coach gets hardcoded strings and an empty API key.
We hit the free-tier limit, so we stubbed it for the demo.

events.reason: Personalisation is the pitch, and the code passes fixed strings to an empty key.

events.text: If a thousand people sign up tomorrow, what breaks first?
Wearable API rate limits. The app itself is live on Base Sepolia and runs today.
We'd move contests to mainnet and scale the Flask server.
FitterCoin doesn't enforce stakes. Every require in joinContest is commented out.
We'd switch them back on before launch.

events.reason: Free entry to a paid contest breaks the business on day one.
Your project doesn't work in production. The live app takes stakes it never holds and pays out bets with nothing.

evidence.label: B · live test f4: winning bet paid 0 ETH

events.text: Which of your claims are you least sure of?
World ID runs on staging mocks until our portal keys land. The app says so.
The AI coach. It works once there's a key.
Go Health Me says World ID verifies humans, but the code uses a mock proof.
It's flagged as staging in the app and in EVALUATE.md. We never claimed it was live.

events.reason: Honest about it, but the claim stays unverified (E5).

events.text: Open gohealthme.app on your phone. It works. That's our whole argument.
We showed the vision. The video speaks for itself.

events.reason: score

1-1.tagline: Two testing pitches. One has tests.

events.text: Describe what your user does in plain English. Our agents turn it into a test that runs on real phones, and fixes itself.
QAgent is the QA engineer you never hired. It reads every PR, clicks through it, and files the bugs.
What happens in the first minute after I sign up?
You type a flow, like 'log in and add to cart', and it runs on a real device.
Connect GitHub and QAgent starts reviewing your next PR.
QAgent's 'Connect GitHub' button does nothing on the live site.
It's a known bug from last night.

events.reason: The first step of the journey fails live.

events.text: Show me the screen I'd live in.
The run view: device, steps, screenshots per step.
The findings dashboard.
QAgent's findings dashboard is a 404 on the live site.
It's behind a feature flag.

events.reason: The screen in the video doesn't exist on the live app.

events.text: How do you know your own product works?
1,232 tests in the repo, and 49 commits at the event with CI on every one.
We dogfood it on our own PRs.
QAgent's explorer returns three canned findings, whatever the app.
That's a fallback while the model warms up.

events.reason: The agent's output is hardcoded.
You sell testing and ship zero tests.

events.text: Why can't a big QA vendor copy you next quarter?
Self-healing on real devices, with vision fallbacks, is years of edge cases.
We're agent-native from day one.
Mozark's 'agents' are keyword automation with a new name.
The fallback chain from XPath to OCR to image match is tested.

events.reason: The self-healing chain is real and tested (E3, E4).

events.text: Who pays, and why now?
QA teams, per seat. They already pay for device farms.
Startups, per repo.
QAgent claims 40 repos tested. There's no log, fixture or report for any of them.
We ran them by hand.

events.reason: No evidence for the traction claim.

events.text: Which claim are you least sure of?
Our API tests use mock tokens. We say so.
None.
Mozark's API tests run on mock tokens.
Correct, and labelled as unit tests.

events.reason: Fair point, honestly owned.

events.text: We tested every project in this arena. Including the one we're fighting.
Imagine what QAgent becomes in a month.

events.reason: score

1-2.tagline: Best code in the room vs. the demo that works.

events.text: Streaming payroll for DAOs, invariant-tested, with clawback that can never touch earned pay.
Split any bill in USDC. Snap the receipt, everyone approves their share in one tap.
Walk me through the core flow on the live app.
Create a vault, deposit, and pay streams every block.
Scan, split, approve. Try it on your phone right now.
Vaultline's deposit returns a 502 on the live app.
The front end points at last week's contract.

events.reason: The first money step fails live.
The demo breaks at deposit. I never saw a stream run.

events.text: Does it work on a phone?
The contributor view does.
Every flow passed on a phone.
After the deposit error, Vaultline's dashboard goes blank.
It recovers on reload.

events.reason: Blank screen after an error is a real UI failure.

events.text: What's the worst thing someone can do to your contract?
Nothing that touches earned pay: five invariants prove it.
Approve less than their share, which the app catches.
Anyone can call SplitSafe's settle().
It only settles when everyone has approved.

events.reason: Open settle() is a real gap, partly mitigated.
Anyone can call settle(). Lock it before mainnet.

events.text: What's new here?
Clawback that's mathematically safe for contributors.
One-tap approval from a photo of a receipt.
Streaming payments are Sablier with a new skin.
Sablier has no clawback cap. Ours is proven.

events.reason: The capped clawback is a real difference.

events.text: What stops this shipping next month?
One contract address.
Nothing. It's live.
Vaultline can't take a deposit today.
It's a one-line fix.

events.reason: Small fix, but the demo still failed.

events.text: Which claim are you least sure of?
One-click deposit. It's broken right now.
Who can settle. We'll lock it.
SplitSafe says only the creator can settle; the code disagrees.
We said we'd lock it.

events.reason: Owned, not fixed.

events.text: The best contracts here. Judge the engine, not the address bug.
It works on your phone today. That's the product.

events.reason: score
